answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x target and confined to the primary region during peak settlement writes. A release went out 2 hours ago, but the regional confinement points away from a bad build (a bad build would degrade all regions). Rolling back mid-peak risks losing in-flight customer writes. Regional failover moves traffic off the degraded primary cleanly — memory_b2 says failover restored latency within minutes during the March degradation, and memory_b1 informs the fallback if failover does not resolve it (rollback becomes the next-window action). Failover preserves writes via replication and does not foreclose the rollback option. Uncertainty remains: if the root cause is the release interacting with regional state, failover may not fully fix it, so I verify both memories before committing.
